findings: Three private identity wrappers distinguish a process-local u64 candidate, an owned DefaultHasher state, and an opaque owned32byte artifact identity. repr(transparent) and derives govern value shape and equality, not algorithm provenance or a persistent encoding for process hashes.

from_hashable borrows T:Hash+?Sized only during new/write/finish. write delegates to the caller type Hash implementation; finish consumes the wrapper and creates an independent candidate. No deterministic cross-version algorithm, secret randomness or collision-free identity is promised.

Actual shaped-cache caller hashes metadata to choose buckets, compares full keys/features, and finally compares exact source_text bytes before accepting a hit. Hash equality alone cannot replace those comparisons.
from_process_hash wraps a caller u64 without rehashing or validation. A bounded rich_cache locator does not justify a complete lifecycle claim about that unowned file.

StableContentDigest::blake3 hashes exact supplied bytes and copies32 resulting bytes. from_bytes and From<[u8;32]> merely wrap arbitrary owned arrays; no algorithm, content-source or cryptographic provenance check is performed.

as_bytes borrows the internal array for the self-borrow lifetime; into_bytes/From return the owned array with byte order unchanged. The wrapper is Copy, so consumption of one value does not invalidate unrelated copies.

Actual SDF variation identity sorts raw tag/value bit pairs and hashes their explicit byte encodings before wrapping. Source font bytes use the blake3 entry. SDF encoding borrows and appends arrays; path hex is a caller format rather than a wrapper validation guarantee.

The three fixed tests contain6assertsites: equality/inequality for selected strings, byte wrapping/roundtrip against the same BLAKE3 library, and size_of checks. They establish neither universal collision absence, an independent cryptographic test vector nor absence of intermediate allocations.
